items.detail: The **Nasdaq** slipped 0.15% to 27,204.38 Tuesday, extending Monday's loss, while the S&P 500 was flat at 7,805.45.
items.why: Chip stocks fell for a fifth straight session, and Applied Materials sank almost 7% on lingering memory-chip worries.

items.detail: Bank earnings got a cool reception: **Citigroup** fell 5.6% and Wells Fargo 3.1%, while JPMorgan's $5.57 a share missed estimates.
items.why: Wells Fargo's interest income fell short, and investors sold Citi even though its profit beat estimates.

items.detail: Brent eased 0.9% to **$105.69** Tuesday, still near three-year highs, ahead of today's CPI report.
items.why: Traders took profits after three days of gains as Saudi pipeline flows to the Red Sea resumed.

items.detail: Korea's **Kospi** rebounded about 1.8% to 6,146 early Wednesday, after closing Tuesday down 5.46% at 6,035.35.
items.why: Bargain hunters bought back Samsung and SK Hynix, though worries about Chinese memory-chip competition still limit confidence.

items.detail: The **Nifty** jumped 1.6% to 22,721.95 Tuesday, more than reversing Monday's fall, as the Sensex climbed 1,109 points.
items.why: HCL Tech's strong results lifted IT stocks 5.2%, and the finance minister offered to hear views on capital-gains taxes.

items.detail: India's **Nifty Smallcap** gained only about **0.1%** Tuesday as the large-cap Nifty rallied 1.6%, flipping Monday's small-cap outperformance.
items.why: The rally was driven by large IT companies, so most of the buying went to big stocks.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** recovered to about **$83,400** Tuesday, up from $81,950 early that day, though it is still stuck below $84,000 ahead of today's CPI.
items.why: Dip buyers stepped in, but traders are wary of risk before the inflation data, which keeps gains limited.

items.detail: **Ether** bounced to about **$2,533** Tuesday after dipping to near $2,411, just above last week's low.
items.why: Leverage in ether futures has fallen 16% in five days, which eased the forced selling.

items.detail: **Solana** held near **$107**, back above its 50-day average after Tuesday's dip.
items.why: A second Hong Kong spot Solana ETF and more asset tokenization on the network helped support the price.

items.detail: **Gold** ended Tuesday near **$4,155**, down about $5, giving up a midday rise to around $4,187.
items.why: A firm dollar and caution before today's US inflation report outweighed the early dip in yields.

crossCuttingTheme: Today's CPI report is the key test: with Brent above $105, a hot reading would raise the odds of another Fed hike, which is why gold and crypto are holding back while chip stocks keep sliding.
